# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 16 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 16 | **Condition:** moderately preserved

---

**16:1** I give thanks to You, O Lord, for You have not abandoned my lot to the assembly of deceit,

**16:2** nor assigned my portion to the council of the concealed.

**16:3** You have summoned me to Your grace and to Your pardon [...]

**16:4** and to the fullness of Your compassion toward all who turn back to You.

**16:5** For You have not set my case before the council of the hidden ones,

**16:6** nor have You reserved truth for the path of the wicked.

**16:7** I know that You have chosen me for [...] and that no one misled by wicked lips will stray from Your way.

**16:8** I know that in Your hand lies the shaping of every spirit, and its function You determined

**16:9** before You brought it into being. How can anyone alter Your decrees?

**16:10** You alone created the righteous; from the womb You prepared him

**16:11** for the appointed time of favor, to be preserved within Your covenant and to walk in all Your ways,

**16:12** and to [...] upon him in the fullness of Your compassion, and to lay open every distress of his soul

**16:13** to eternal deliverance and unending peace without want. You have exalted his honor

**16:14** above all flesh.

**16:15** But the wicked You created for the hour of Your wrath, and from the womb You set them apart

**16:16** for the day of carnage. For they tread a path that is not good,

**16:17** and they have spurned Your covenant, and their soul has abhorred Your truth.

**16:18** They took no pleasure in all You commanded, and they chose what You detest.

**16:19** According to the mysteries of Your understanding You have [...] all their recompense

**16:20** for Your judgments, to carry out judgment upon them before all Your works,

**16:21** that they may stand as a sign and a portent for everlasting ages, that all may acknowledge Your glory

**16:22** and Your surpassing might. What then is flesh, that it should comprehend these things?

**16:23** How does a vessel of clay fathom wonders? He lies in iniquity from the womb,

**16:24** and until old age in faithless guilt. I know

**16:25** that no mortal possesses righteousness, and the blameless way belongs to no son of man.

**16:26** To God Most High belong all righteous deeds, and the way of man stands firm

**16:27** only through the spirit God has fashioned for him, to perfect a path for the children of men,

**16:28** that all His creatures may know the power of His might and the abundance of His compassion

**16:29** toward all the children of His favor.

**16:30** As for me, awe of You has taken hold of me, shuddering and trembling have gripped me,

**16:31** and all my bones declare [...] and my heart has dissolved like wax before fire,

**16:32** and my knees [...] for I recall my guilt and the faithlessness of my forebears.

**16:33** The wicked rose against Your covenant, the worthless against Your word.

**16:34** I said: On account of my transgression I am banished far from Your covenant.

**16:35** But when I remember the power of Your hand and the multitude of Your mercies, I rise.

**16:36** I stand, and my spirit holds firm against the blow, for I rest upon Your lovingkindness

**16:37** and the fullness of Your mercies, for You pardon iniquity and cleanse a mortal of guilt through Your righteousness.

---
*LOGOS notes: Column 16 develops the Qumran doctrine of double predestination (lines 10-18). The parallel with 1QS III-IV is unmistakable. The final section (30-37) closely reprises Column 11's emotional arc.*
